questions.question: The marked price of a chair is 20 percent more than its cost price. If the chair is sold for Rs. 220 after a discount of Rs. 20, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:

Marked price of the chair = 20% more than cost price

Selling price after discount = Rs. 220

Discount given = Rs. 20

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price = Cost Price + 20% of Cost Price

Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

Profit Percentage = [(Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price] × 100

Let Cost Price be Rs. x

Marked Price = x + 0.20x = 1.20x

Selling Price = 220

Discount = 20

Marked Price = Selling Price + Discount

⇒ 1.20x = 220 + 20

⇒ 1.20x = 240

⇒ x = 240 / 1.20

⇒ x = 200

Cost Price = Rs. 200

Selling Price = Rs. 220

Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price

Profit = 220 - 200

Profit = 20

Profit Percentage = (20 / 200) × 100

⇒ Profit Percentage = 10%

**The profit percentage is 10%.**

pq = (1 + 1/√2) × (1 − 1/√2) = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Be it a consequence of the shifting tectonic plates or the result of volcanic activity, / (2) the geological formation of the archipelago is much more complex than / (3) any other island chain in the Pacific basin, as recently suggested / (4) by the research published in the journal of Earth Sciences.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Part 3 .

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Logical Comparison:** This sentence contains an error of **Illogical Comparison**. When we use words like "more than" or "as...as," we must compare like with like.
 
• **Error Identification:** Part 2 mentions the "geological formation." Part 3 compares this directly to "any other island chain." One cannot compare a geological process to a geographical landmass.
 
• **Evaluating the Fix:**
 
 
• Incorrect: ...formation... is more complex than any other island chain.
 
• Correct: ...formation... is more complex than **that of** any other island chain. (Here, 'that' refers back to 'formation').
 
 
 
• **Conclusion:** Part 3 is grammatically incomplete because it lacks the pronoun 'that of' to balance the comparison.
 
• **Correct Sentence: ***Be it a consequence of the shifting tectonic plates or the result of volcanic activity, the geological formation of the archipelago is much more complex than **that of** any other island chain in the Pacific basin, as recently suggested by the research published in the journal of Earth Sciences.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules of Comparison:**

 
 
• Singular comparison: Use **"that of"** (e.g., The climate of India is hotter than that of* England).
 
• Plural comparison: Use **"those of"** (e.g., The streets of Delhi are wider than *those of* Mumbai).
 
 
 
• **Vocabulary:**
 
 
• **Archipelago (Hindi meaning: द्वीपसमूह - Dweep-samuh):** A group of islands.
 
• **Tectonic Plates (Hindi meaning: विवर्तनिक प्लेटें - Vivartanik plates):** Massive, irregularly shaped slabs of solid rock that make up the Earth's lithosphere.
 
• **Consequence (Hindi meaning: परिणाम - Parinam):** A result or effect of an action or condition.

• The basic rules for changing or ____converting direct speech into indirect speech__:

 __
 
• ​Remove comma and inverted commas.
 
• The conjunction 'that' is used in place of commas and inverted commas.
 
• If the **reporting verb** is in the present tense, change it into the corresponding past tense. If it is in the simple past tense, change it into the past perfect tense.
 
 
 
• Here, "said to" in "direct speech" is changed into 'requested' in "indirect speech" as 'please' is used in the direct speech which is used as a polite addition to requests, commands.
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as "He requested his father to increase his pocket-money."

• If the first part of the sentence (reporting verb part) belongs to the past tense, the tense of reported speech will change. If the first part of the sentence (reporting verb part) belongs to the present or future tense, the tense of reported speech will not change.
 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
 Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 
 
 

 

**EXTRA BITES**__**:**

 
• When the reporting verb expresses a universal truth, we do not normally change it into the past tense.
 For example:
 
 
• Direct Speech: The President said, ‘*All people have equal rights*.’
 Indirect Speech: The President said *that all people have equal rights*.
 
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the present or future tense, we do not change the tense of the reporting verb.
 ​For example:​
 
 
• Direct Speech: He says*, 'I will come.'*
 Indirect Speech:* *He says* that he will come.*

Consider the following statements regarding Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-nomadic Tribes (DNTs):

I. They emerged as a legal category after the repeal of the Criminal Tribes Act, 1871, and currently lack recognition under any separate constitutional Schedule.

II. The Census of India Act, 1948 statutorily mandates a distinct enumeration column for Denotified Tribes in every decennial Census.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1 **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-nomadic Tribes have demanded a separate Census column and constitutional recognition through a distinct Schedule, citing decades of misclassification within SC/ST/OBC categories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Denotified Tribes came to be identified after the repeal of the Criminal Tribes Act in 1952 and do not have a distinct constitutional Schedule under Articles 341 or 342. **Hence, Statement I is correct. **
 
• The Census of India Act, 1948 provides the legal framework for conducting the Census but does not mandate a separate statutory column for Denotified Tribes; the inclusion of such a column is an executive/administrative choice. **Hence, Statement II is incorrect. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Which of the following is/are characteristic features of wind-eroded landforms in desert regions?**

1.Formation of mushroom-shaped rocks with a slender base and broad upper cap

2.Development of flat-topped residual hills resembling table surfaces

3.Emergence of rock remnants standing as isolated pedestals
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3 all are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mushroom-shaped rocks**, also known as pedestal rocks, are formed due to wind abrasion, where the lower portion erodes more quickly due to the concentration of sand particles near the ground. This creates a slender base and a broad cap.
 
• **Flat-topped residual hills**, resembling table surfaces, are called mesas. These are formed due to differential erosion in desert regions, leaving behind such flat-topped landforms.
 
• **Rock remnants standing as isolated pedestals**, or inselbergs, are created due to the erosional activities of wind, which remove the surrounding softer material, leaving harder rock remnants.
 
• Wind erosion is a predominant geomorphic process in desert regions and creates unique landforms such as yardangs, dunes, and deflation hollows.
 
• These features are characteristic of arid and semi-arid desert landscapes where wind plays a significant role in shaping the topography.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wind Erosion and Desert Landforms**

 
 
• Wind erosion occurs primarily in arid regions due to the lack of vegetation cover and the abundance of loose, fine-grained particles that can be transported by wind.
 
• Common processes include deflation (removal of loose particles), abrasion (grinding of rock surfaces by windborne particles), and attrition (collision between particles).
 
• Desert landforms shaped by wind include dunes, yardangs, ventifacts, and blowouts.
 
 
 
• **Pedestal Rocks or Mushroom-shaped Rocks**
 
 
• These are formed due to differential erosion by wind, where the softer material at the base erodes faster than the harder upper layers.
 
• Such landforms are commonly found in arid zones and are indicative of wind abrasion near the surface.
 
 
 
• **Mesas and Buttes**
 
 
• Mesas are flat-topped hills with steep sides, formed due to erosion of sedimentary rock layers.
 
• Buttes are similar to mesas but smaller in size and are often remnants of larger mesas.
 
• Both are features of arid landscapes and result from the differential erosion of rock layers.
 
 
 
• **Inselbergs**
 
 
• Inselbergs are isolated rock outcrops that rise abruptly from the surrounding plains.
 
• They are formed due to the prolonged erosion of softer surrounding material, leaving behind hard rock masses.
 
• Examples include Uluru in Australia and Sugarloaf Mountain in Brazil.

__

It is also part of the **Khuddaka Nikaya**. Hence, the association with **Khuddaka Nikaya is correct. **

Thus, the texts **Jataka and Dhammapada are included in the Khuddaka Nikaya → Option D. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Sutta Pitaka** is divided into **five Nikayas**: ** Digha Nikaya** – long discourses of the Buddha. ** Majjhima Nikaya **– middle-length discourses. ** Samyutta Nikaya** – grouped or connected discourses arranged by theme. ** Anguttara Nikaya **– numerical discourses arranged according to numbers. **Khuddaka Nikaya **– a miscellaneous collection of shorter texts.

• **Vocationalisation of education: **The Commission recommended that vocational education be integrated into the school curriculum to make it more job-oriented.
 
• **Expansion of higher education: **The Commission recommended the establishment of new universities and colleges and expanding existing institutions to meet the growing demand for higher education.
 
• **Educational planning: **The Commission recommended setting up a National Education Commission and State Education Commission to prepare long-term educational plans and policies.
 
• **Promotion of Indian languages: **The Commission recommended that the study of Indian languages should be given greater importance and that they should be used as a medium of instruction at the primary level.
 
• **Use of educational technology: **The Commission recommended using educational technology, such as radio and television, to disseminate education.

**Consider the following statements: **

1. The Governor can dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

2. The President has no such power regarding the Lok Sabha. Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state has the constitutional authority to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly under Article 174(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution, usually on the advice of the Chief Minister or in certain circumstances like a no-confidence motion.
 
• The President of India, on the other hand, has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution. Therefore, Statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• The dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly is an executive action of the Governor and is generally done to pave the way for fresh elections.
 
• The President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• Thus, only Statement 1 is correct, as the Governor has the power to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role and Powers:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the state's Chief Minister and Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor can summon, prorogue, or dissolve the State Legislative Assembly under Article 174 of the Constitution.
 
• In extraordinary circumstances (e.g., no-confidence motion passed), the Governor can dissolve the assembly without the advice of the Chief Minister, but this is subject to judicial review.
 
 
 
• **President's Power to Dissolve Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The President of India can dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85(2)(b) of the Constitution.
 
• This power is exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The dissolution of the Lok Sabha paves the way for general elections in the country.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Dissolution and Prorogation:**
 
 
• **Dissolution:** Refers to the complete termination of the current House of Parliament or State Legislative Assembly. It necessitates fresh elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Discussing the other layers of the TCP/IP layers below:

 
• **Physical layer: **The first layer of the OSI model builds the physical connection between the devices. The information is divided into small bits and then transfer from one device to another.
 
• **Data link layer:** This layer is the second layer of the OSI model. Here, data is transferred from node to node.
 
• **Internet layer: **This layer is the third layer of the TCP model. It transfers the data frame from one host of a network to another host of another network. The Internet layer includes the powerful Internet Protocol (IP), the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP), and the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP).
 
• **Transport layer: **This layer is the fourth layer of the OSI model. This layer uses TCP\IP and UDP protocols for transmitting the data.
 
• **Application layer: **This layer is the seventh layer or the top layer of the OSI model. In this layer, humans can interact with the system through different applications and are also able to connect with the network. High-level protocols are used in this layer for managing data transmission and networking.

 

The **OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) **model is a conceptual framework used to understand and implement computer networking protocols in seven distinct layers. Each layer has specific functions and communicates with the layers directly above and below it. Here is a brief definition and some important information about each layer:

 
• **Physical Layer (Layer 1)**

 
 
• Definition: This layer is concerned with the transmission of raw bit streams over a physical medium.
 
• Important Information: It deals with hardware elements (such as switches, cables, and network adapters), electrical signals, and physical data rates. It defines the means of sending and receiving data bits across a network.
 
 
 
• **Data Link Layer (Layer 2)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides node-to-node data transfer—a link between two directly connected nodes.
 
• Important Information: It handles error detection and correction from the physical layer, frame synchronization, and flow control. The Data Link Layer is divided into two sublayers: the Media Access Control (MAC) layer and the Logical Link Control (LLC) layer.
 
 
 
• **Network Layer (Layer 3)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer is responsible for packet forwarding including routing through different routers.
 
• Important Information: It handles logical addressing (IP addresses), routing, and path determination. Protocols like IP (Internet Protocol), ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol), and ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) operate at this layer.
 
 
 
• **Transport Layer (Layer 4)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides reliable data transfer services to the upper layers.
 
• Important Information: It ensures complete data transfer, error recovery, and flow control. Two main protocols in this layer are TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and UDP (User Datagram Protocol).
 
 
 
• **Session Layer (Layer 5)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer establishes, manages, and terminates connections between applications.
 
• Important Information: It handles session setup, coordination, and termination between networked devices. It is responsible for dialog control and synchronization.
 
 
 
• **Presentation Layer (Layer 6)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer translates data between the application layer and the network format.
 
• Important Information: It handles data encryption, decryption, data compression, and data translation. This layer ensures that data is in a usable format and is encoded and decoded properly.
 
 
 
• **Application Layer (Layer 7)**
 
 
• Definition: This layer provides network services directly to the user's software applications.
 
• Important Information: It handles application services for file transfers, email, and other network software services. Protocols at this layer include HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol), FTP (File Transfer Protocol), SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol), and DNS (Domain Name System).

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the first generation of computers?

options.text: Machine language and the use of symbols in instructions
More reliable and less prone to hardware failure
Use of vacuum tubes to build circuits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The first generation of computers used vacuum tubes to build circuits.**
 
• These computers generated large amounts of heat due to the use of vacuum tubes.
 
• **Machine language and symbols were used for instructions in this generation.**
 
• However, these computers were not more reliable and were highly prone to hardware failure due to the limitations of vacuum tube technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Generation Computers:** These computers were introduced in the late 1940s and used vacuum tubes for processing. They were bulky, consumed a lot of power, and had limited reliability.
 
• **Second Generation Computers:** Transistors replaced vacuum tubes, making computers smaller, faster, and more reliable.
 
• **Third Generation Computers:** Integrated circuits further improved reliability and speed while reducing size and cost.
 
• **Fourth Generation Computers:** Microprocessors were introduced, leading to the development of personal computers.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a cache in a computer system?

options.text: To protect against viruses and worms
To improve the performance by storing frequently accessed data

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To improve the performance by storing frequently accessed data.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A cache is a smaller, faster memory located close to the CPU or integrated into the CPU itself.**
 
• It stores frequently accessed data or instructions to reduce the time required for fetching them from the main memory.
 
• **The purpose of the cache is to improve system performance by minimizing delays caused by slower memory access.**
 
• There are different levels of cache memory, such as L1 (Level 1), L2 (Level 2), and L3 (Level 3), each varying in size and proximity to the CPU.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Memory:** The main memory (RAM) is larger but slower compared to the cache. It stores data temporarily while the system is running.
 
• **Virtual Memory:** Virtual memory is a section of the hard drive used as an extension of RAM to store data that cannot fit into physical memory.
 
• **Storage:** Permanent storage devices like hard drives or SSDs are used to store data persistently, but they are slower compared to cache memory.
 
• **Cache Hit:** A cache hit occurs when the required data is found in the cache, reducing access time.
 
• **Cache Miss:** A cache miss happens when the required data is not found in the cache, and it has to be fetched from the main memory.

Phishing 

__
 
• It is cyber-attacks are the practice of sending fraudulent communications that appear to come from a reputable source. It is usually done through email.
 
• It is a **type of cyber attack** that involves **tricking users into revealing sensitive information. *Hence, Option 1 is correct.***
 
• The goal is to steal sensitive data like credit card and login information or to install malware on the victim’s machine.
 
• The first phishing lawsuit was filed in 2004 against a Californian teenager who created the imitation of the website “America Online”. With this fake website, he was able to gain sensitive information from users and access their credit card details to withdraw money from their accounts.
 
• Other than email and website phishing, there’s also 'vishing' (voice phishing), 'smishing' (SMS Phishing), and several other phishing techniques cybercriminals are constantly coming up with.

• It is a type of** injection attack **that makes it** possible to execute malicious SQL statements.** These statements control a database server behind a web application. Attackers can use SQL Injection vulnerabilities to bypass application security measures.

• A **denial-of-service (DoS) attack** is a type of cyber attack in which a **malicious actor aims to render a computer or other device unavailable **to its intended users by interrupting the device's normal functioning.
